title: Dijkstra's shortest path algorithm
summary: Dijkstra finds the shortest path from a source vertex to all other vertices in a weighted graph with non-negative edge weights. Uses a priority queue (min-heap) of (distance, vertex). Greedy: always process the vertex with smallest tentative distance. Relax edges: if dist[u] + w(u,v) < dist[v], update dist[v]. O((V+E) log V) with binary heap, O(E + V log V) with Fibonacci heap.

A* adds a heuristic h(v) to the priority: f(v) = g(v) + h(v). Admissible heuristic (h(v) ≤ actual cost) guarantees optimality.

notes: Dijkstra requires non-negative edge weights. Negative weights need Bellman-Ford.
Dijkstra is used in GPS navigation, network routing (OSPF), and game AI.
A* is Dijkstra with a heuristic. Used in pathfinding (games, robotics).
Bidirectional Dijkstra searches from both source and target. Faster in practice.
Fibonacci heap gives better theoretical complexity but is slower in practice due to constant factors.
